blocks.explanation:
A double equality: we must show the product equals two different expressions.
Expand the product, then replace squares using \(\sin^2 + \cos^2 = 1\) in two different ways.
Plan: expand, multiply (difference of squares), then convert.
steps:
Given: the statement.
To show: \(\cos(\alpha + \beta)\cos(\alpha - \beta) = \cos^2\alpha - \sin^2\beta\) and also \(= \cos^2\beta - \sin^2\alpha\).
Method: \(\cos(\alpha \pm \beta)\) formulas, \((x - y)(x + y) = x^2 - y^2\), and \(\sin^2 x + \cos^2 x = 1\).

Expand both factors
\[\text{L.H.S.} = (\cos\alpha\cos\beta - \sin\alpha\sin\beta)\]
\[\times(\cos\alpha\cos\beta + \sin\alpha\sin\beta)\]
Why: Sum and difference formulas for cosine.

Difference of squares
\[= \cos^2\alpha\cos^2\beta - \sin^2\alpha\sin^2\beta\]
Why: \((x - y)(x + y) = x^2 - y^2\) with \(x = \cos\alpha\cos\beta\), \(y = \sin\alpha\sin\beta\).

First form: replace \(\cos^2\beta\) and \(\sin^2\alpha\)
\[= \cos^2\alpha(1 - \sin^2\beta) - (1 - \cos^2\alpha)\sin^2\beta\]
\[= \cos^2\alpha - \cos^2\alpha\sin^2\beta\]
\[- \sin^2\beta + \cos^2\alpha\sin^2\beta\]
\[= \cos^2\alpha - \sin^2\beta\]
Why: \(\cos^2\beta = 1 - \sin^2\beta\), \(\sin^2\alpha = 1 - \cos^2\alpha\); the mixed terms cancel.

Second form: replace \(\cos^2\alpha\) and \(\sin^2\beta\)
\[= (1 - \sin^2\alpha)\cos^2\beta - \sin^2\alpha(1 - \cos^2\beta)\]
\[= \cos^2\beta - \sin^2\alpha\cos^2\beta\]
\[- \sin^2\alpha + \sin^2\alpha\cos^2\beta\]
\[= \cos^2\beta - \sin^2\alpha\]
Why: Start again from the step 3 result and replace the other pair; the mixed terms cancel again.

Check with \(\alpha = 60^{\circ}\), \(\beta = 30^{\circ}\)
\[\cos 90^{\circ}\cos 30^{\circ} = 0\]
\[\cos^2 60^{\circ} - \sin^2 30^{\circ} = \dfrac{1}{4} - \dfrac{1}{4} = 0\]
\[\cos^2 30^{\circ} - \sin^2 60^{\circ} = \dfrac{3}{4} - \dfrac{3}{4} = 0 \;\checkmark\]
Why: All three expressions agree.
